author: implementation-agent

findings.summary: Unquoted url(...) scanning stops at escaped closing parentheses and can corrupt valid CSS asset references.
findings.consequence: A managed Reader stylesheet reference such as url(images/foo\).png) is valid CSS for a filename containing a closing parenthesis, but rebasing turns it into url(/red/css/images/foo/).png), so that asset URL no longer points at the intended file.
findings.evidence: The owned loop delegates every candidate token to rebaseStylesheetToken at line 146. Its unquoted url(...) dependency locates the end with stylesheet.indexOf(")", referenceStart), so it treats an escaped \) as the token close, then passes the truncated reference through new URL, which normalizes the trailing backslash into a slash. The named tests cover quoted strings, comments, basic quoted and unquoted urls, and absolute/data/hash references, but not escaped characters inside unquoted url(...) values.
findings.recommendation: Parse unquoted url(...) bodies character by character and treat backslash escapes as part of the reference, or conservatively leave unquoted url(...) tokens containing backslashes unchanged while still rebasing ordinary unescaped relative URLs.
